description:
Store and manage content in your MIND knowledge graph. Use for facts, decisions, learnings, research, notes — anything worth remembering. Auto-categorized. Always log outcomes here after completing tasks. Supports create (default), delete, search, get, and list.

⚠️ PRIVATE vs PUBLIC: `document` and `entry` are PRIVATE to the user's knowledge graph. `feed_post` is a PUBLIC social-media post that appears on the user's public feed for everyone to see. Default to `entry` for all agent outcomes, logs, decisions, and research. NEVER use `feed_post` unless the user explicitly says "post", "share", "tweet", "feed", or "thought to my feed" — deploy logs, PR notes, work outcomes, and agent activity belong in `entry`, NOT on the public feed.

Title rule: titles are plain natural language, written as a person would name the thing. No type prefixes ("Journal Entry", "Agent Entry", "Document"), no ids or hashes, no ISO timestamps; never put '/' or parentheses in a title, the card is derived from it. Lessons keep the 'Lesson - Failure - <behavior>' / 'Lesson - Behavior - <behavior>' / 'Lesson - Win - <behavior>' shape exactly as written (MIND never rewrites a lesson title) and files them under Lessons.

FILING: every write is filed, nothing lands loose. Pass `folder` (a folder id, a folder name, or a 'Parent/Child' path) when you know where it belongs; otherwise leave it out and MIND files it by what it is (agent entries, automation logs, lessons, mistakes, decisions, documents). An explicit folder always wins; a secure folder is refused. One living document per entity: when a person, project, focus, calendar event or recurring job already has a record, update that record (mind_crm, mind_life, mind_focuses) or supersede the earlier note with `supersedes`; do not write a new entry that restates it.

WRITE FOR THE AGENT WHO WILL SEARCH FOR THIS LATER — retrieval quality is decided here, not at query time. State facts in the words someone will later search for. Put the entity name in the first sentence. Inline dates, ids, file paths and numbers rather than saying "the PR" or "yesterday" — a note that only says "fixed it" is unfindable. If this supersedes an earlier note, say so explicitly and name what it replaces, so the older fact can be closed off instead of silently competing with this one.

action.description: Action: create (store new content — default), delete (remove by ID), search (find entries), get (retrieve by ID), list (paginated listing)

content.description: What to remember — the actual content to store (required for create)

folder.description: Where to file this write: a folder id, a folder name, or a 'Parent/Child' path (mind_folders list shows them). Optional: omit it and MIND files the write by what it is. An explicit folder always wins; a secure folder is refused. Applies to documents and entries.

limit.description: Max items to return for list/search

supersedes.description: Entries only: earlier records of yours this entry replaces, by id, exact title, or the exact reference title retrieval shows (e.g. "Agent Entry: <title>"; older entries show "Journal Entry: <title>"). They are tagged superseded, never deleted, and stop being retrieved once the server enables it. Use it whenever you record a fix, reversal or newer version, so MIND stops serving the old fact.

title.description: Title for documents and entries: plain natural language, no type prefixes, no ids (auto-generated if omitted for feed posts)

type.description: Storage type. PRIVATE: `document` (long-form, structured — research, specs, strategies), `entry` (medium — observations, findings, action logs, agent outcomes — DEFAULT for agent work). PUBLIC: `feed_post` (a social-media-style post that appears on the user's PUBLIC feed for everyone to see — NEVER use unless the user explicitly said "post", "share", "tweet", "feed", or "thought to my feed"). `thought` is a deprecated alias for `feed_post` and behaves identically — prefer `feed_post` for clarity.

name: mind_remember
